cycle.label: Reporting period
cycle.note: Florida CPE periods run July 1 – June 30, every two years.

requirements.label: Total CPE
requirements.note: Missed June 30? Florida allows an automatic extension to September 15 with 8 extra accounting & auditing hours, or to December 31 with 16 extra.

requirements.label: Behavioral
requirements.note: Maximum, not a target. No more than 20 behavioral hours (communications, personal development, practice administration) count toward the 80.

requirements.label: Governmental (Yellow Book audits)
requirements.note: 24 hours of governmental CPE if you work on audits under Government Auditing Standards.

requirements.label: Florida Board-approved ethics
requirements.note: 4 hours from a Florida Board-approved ethics provider, covering Chapters 455 and 473, F.S. We count courses with "Florida" and "ethics" (or "473") in the title — edit the title if yours isn't picked up.

newLicensee.note: Your first Florida CPE period runs from your license issue date to the third June 30 after it.

licenseDateHint: Florida CPE periods end June 30 every two years (e.g. 06/30/2027). This is separate from your license renewal date.
issueDateHint: If you were licensed recently, your first period runs from this date to the third June 30 after it.
limitsNotTracked: Self-study in A&A or technical business must be from NASBA QAS sponsors.
Published articles/books: max 20 hours per period.
toVerify: Rule 61H1-33.003 was amended effective 9/30/2026 ('clarify renewal deadline language') — confirm nothing changes the 80 / 8 / 4 / 20 figures or the June 30 period.

Mapping of NASBA fields to Florida's behavioral vs technical business subjects (Business Management and Organization, Production and Behavioral Ethics treated as behavioral; Computer Software and Applications as technical business).
